blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, King Herod had already put the apostle James to death. When he saw how that pleased the crowd, he arrested Peter too, and meant to bring him out for trial after the Passover. Sixteen soldiers guarded him.

verses.text: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, prayer was made. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Prayer was made"] Prayer was made. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "Prayer was made"] Peter was in prison, but the church was on its knees.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Peter was in prison. But. The church was praying. Without ceasing. They could not break down the prison door. So they went to the One who could.

verses.text: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Look at Peter. Chained between two soldiers, the night before he might die, and he is sleeping. That is peace.

verses.text: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.

verses.text: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And so he did. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.

blocks.text: They were still praying. Middle of the night, and the house was full of folks praying for Peter.

verses.text: And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda.

verses.text: And when she knew Peter’s voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Rhoda was a young servant girl. She heard that voice and got so excited she forgot to open the gate. She ran in to tell everybody.

verses.text: And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she constantly affirmed that it was even so. Then said they, It is his angel.

segments.speaker: narrator

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, they were praying for Peter to get out, and when he got out, they told the girl she was crazy. But Rhoda would not back down. She kept saying, it is him. It is him.

verses.text: But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened the door, and saw him, they were astonished.

segments.speaker: narrator

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: And Peter just kept on knocking.

verses.text: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Thank God for the prayer meeting. Thank God for folks who pray in the night when the news is bad. And thank God for Rhoda, the young one nobody believed, who knew the answer when she heard it at the gate. Sometimes God answers while we are still praying. Keep praying. And when the knock comes, open the door.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Acts 12:5-17; the angel read by the narrator; James's death (12:2) told in our own words; no promise that every prayer is answered this way.

cultural.note: Rhoda, the young servant nobody believed, honoured; the prayer meeting tradition warm and real; 'prayer was made' at the turn.
